title: The Adorned: Corrupted Magic Jewel Amplifier, Effect Breakpoints and Crafting (0.5.4)
summary: The Adorned is a Unique Diamond Jewel in Path of Exile 2 0.5.4 that grants (0-150)% increased Effect of Jewel Socket Passive Skills containing Corrupted Magic Jewels. This guide covers which jewels qualify, the effect breakpoints at 50/75/100/125/150%, the Magic Jewel corrupting workflow, the 0.4.0 change from the legacy 0-100% range, the Trialmaster drop, valuation, and community questions.
description: How The Adorned works in PoE2 0.5.4: the Diamond Jewel that amplifies Corrupted Magic Jewels in your passive tree, effect breakpoint math, Magic Jewel crafting, legacy 0-100% versus current 0-150%, Trialmaster drop, and trade value.
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team
imageAlt: Path of Exile 2 The Adorned unique Diamond Jewel amplifying Corrupted Magic Jewels socketed in the passive skill tree

sections.title: Quick answer
sections.callout: The Adorned is a Unique Diamond Jewel that grants (0-150)% increased Effect of Jewel Socket Passive Skills containing Corrupted Magic Jewels. It multiplies the effect of every Corrupted Magic Jewel (a blue, two-modifier jewel that has been corrupted) sitting in a jewel socket inside its radius on the passive tree. It does nothing for Rare, Unique, or uncorrupted jewels, and it cannot affect itself. In 0.5.4 it drops only from the Trialmaster, the capstone boss of the Trial of Chaos.
calloutDetail: The roll is random between 0% and 150%; a perfect 150% roll makes each qualifying jewel roughly 2.5x as strong.
The jewel is already Corrupted on drop, so the increased-effect value is locked - you cannot Divine or Vaal the roll normally.

answers.label: Use for
text: Scaling a passive tree that runs several high-value Corrupted Magic Jewels (life, resistances, attributes, or your key damage stat).

answers.label: Check first
text: Confirm the jewels you plan to amplify are Magic (not Rare/Unique) and Corrupted, and read the current 0-150% range before overpaying for a legacy 0-100% copy.

answers.label: Avoid
text: Assuming it boosts Rare or Unique jewels, equipment sockets, or Sinister Jewel Sockets - it affects only Corrupted Magic Jewels in passive-tree sockets in radius.

sections.title: Family overview: Diamond Unique Jewels
intro: The Adorned belongs to the Diamond Unique Jewel family - special jewels that rewrite how a passive-tree jewel socket behaves rather than granting flat stats. Each member solves a different tree problem.

sections.title: Effect breakpoints (50 / 75 / 100 / 125 / 150%)
sections.caption: Formula: amplified mod = floor( base mod x (1 + roll / 100) ). Base mods without decimals are floored to the nearest integer. Example jewel mod: +12% increased Maximum Life.

cells.note: Half-again bonus over the base jewel

sections.note: Because the game floors intermediate results, the practical bonus is monotonic but stepwise; a detailed per-value breakpoint spreadsheet exists on the wiki. Flat values scale the same way: a Corrupted Magic Jewel granting +20 to Maximum Life becomes +50 Life at 150%.

sections.title: Overview and current versus legacy
paragraphs: The Adorned turns a specific category of jewel into a multiplier. Its single line, (0-150)% increased Effect of Jewel Socket Passive Skills containing Corrupted Magic Jewels, applies to every Corrupted Magic Jewel socketed in a jewel socket that falls inside the Adorned's radius on the passive tree. A Magic Jewel is the blue-rarity jewel with exactly two modifiers; once corrupted (typically with a Vaal Orb) it qualifies, and the Adorned scales the effect of that socket's passives by up to 2.5x at a perfect roll.

Because it multiplies, The Adorned rewards a tree that invests in several high-value Corrupted Magic Jewels. One weak jewel barely moves the needle; a tree loaded with well-corrupted Magic Jewels makes The Adorned one of the largest single-slot power spikes in the game.

Current versus legacy: in the current 0.5.4 range the roll is random between 0% and 150%. Before patch 0.4.0 the range was 0-100%, so older copies cap at a 2x multiplier. A modern 150% roll is strictly stronger than any legacy copy. The Adorned also cannot affect itself, Rare jewels, Unique jewels, Time-Lost jewels used as the radius anchor, jewels socketed into equipment (for example Sekhema's Resolve), or jewels inside Sinister Jewel Sockets - those are not passive-tree jewel sockets.
bullets: Current (0.5.4): random roll between 0% and 150% increased effect.
Legacy (pre-0.4.0): random roll between 0% and 100% increased effect.
Only Corrupted Magic Jewels in passive-tree sockets in radius are amplified.
The jewel is Corrupted on drop; the roll is locked and cannot be Divined or Vaal-rerolled.

sections.title: Usage: corrupting and socketing Magic Jewels

steps.label: Choose a Diamond base and target mods
body: Pick Magic Jewels (blue, two modifiers) whose pair of stats is strong for your build: life, resistances, attributes, or your key damage stat. Quality the jewel first with a catalyst if relevant.

steps.label: Corrupt the Magic Jewels
body: Use a Vaal Orb to corrupt each Magic Jewel. Corruption can improve, brick, or leave the jewel unchanged, and may add a third implicit modifier. Corrupt spares so you keep usable copies.

steps.label: Confirm the jewels are still Magic and Corrupted
body: The Adorned only amplifies Corrupted Magic Jewels. A jewel that stopped being Magic, or was never corrupted, contributes nothing.

steps.label: Plan and allocate a socket inside the radius
body: Place The Adorned in an allocated jewel socket, then allocate nearby sockets for your Corrupted Magic Jewels inside its radius. Remember you still pay the passive points to reach and allocate those sockets.

steps.label: Search for ready Corrupted Magic Jewels on trade
body: If crafting is slow, search the trade site for Corrupted Magic Jewels (Item Category: Jewel, Rarity: Magic, Stat filters for your two target mods, Corrupted: Yes) and buy the pair you need rather than corrupting blindly.

before: A +12% Maximum Life Magic Jewel contributes +12% Life on its own.
after: With a 150% Adorned, the same jewel behaves like +30% Maximum Life, and every other qualifying jewel scales the same way.
compare.note: The multiplier compounds across all Corrupted Magic Jewels in radius, which is why The Adorned rewards multiple quality jewels rather than one.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: These are the failures that make players think The Adorned 'does nothing'. Most come from confusing which jewels qualify or misreading the roll.
bullets: Using a Rare Jewel - only Magic (blue, two-mod) jewels are amplified; Rare and Unique jewels get nothing.
Forgetting to corrupt - the jewel must be Corrupted; an uncorrupted Magic Jewel is ignored.
Running a single low-value Magic Jewel - one weak jewel barely moves the needle; The Adorned rewards multiple quality jewels.
Reading 150% as 150% more - it is +150% increased Effect, i.e. x2.5, not a flat +150 absolute value.
Ignoring the pathing cost - you still pay passive points to reach and allocate the socket.
Copying old 0-100% breakpoints - the current 0.5.4 range reaches 150%; legacy tables undervalue modern rolls.

sections.title: Alternatives
paragraphs: A Rare or well-rolled Diamond Jewel can deliver flat life, resistances, attributes and utility suffixes that The Adorned does not provide, at the cost of the multiplier. If your tree is not built around Corrupted Magic Jewels, a normal jewel is often the better value.

Other Diamond Uniques trade the amplifier for specialised payoffs (random radius, remote Keystone, ring allocation, or random Notables). They suit narrower builds and should be considered only when Corrupted Magic Jewel scaling is not your priority.
Catalysts and the Charms guide are complementary systems rather than replacements; they do not change The Adorned's effect range.
bullets: Rare Diamond Jewel: flexible suffixes, no multiplier.
Other Diamond Uniques: build-specific, weaker for magic-jewel scaling.

entries.question: Why does my The Adorned show no effect after socketing a jewel?
summary: A player reported that equipping The Adorned changed nothing on their character sheet.
editorialAnalysis: The Adorned only amplifies Corrupted Magic Jewels in passive-tree sockets inside its radius. A Rare jewel, an uncorrupted Magic Jewel, a jewel in equipment, or a jewel outside the radius contributes nothing.
officialAnswer: Only Corrupted Magic Jewels in radius are amplified; verify the jewel type and position before concluding the item is broken.

entries.question: Does The Adorned work with Rare or Unique jewels?
summary: A guide summarised which jewels benefit from the multiplier.
editorialAnalysis: Only Magic (blue, two-modifier) jewels that have been corrupted are amplified. Rare jewels (3-4 mods) and Unique jewels, including The Adorned itself, are unaffected.
officialAnswer: Amplifies Corrupted Magic Jewels only; Rare and Unique jewels get no bonus.

entries.question: Can I Divine or Vaal The Adorned to improve the roll?
summary: A guide explained why the roll cannot be rerolled.
editorialAnalysis: The Adorned drops already Corrupted, so the increased-effect value is locked at drop. A Vaal Cultivation Orb (added in 0.4.0b) can add extra modifiers but does not change the base increased-effect roll.
officialAnswer: The base roll is fixed on drop; only Vaal Cultivation can add side modifiers.

entries.question: Is a 150% roll really 2.5x my magic jewels?
summary: A video showcased a tree built entirely around The Adorned.
editorialAnalysis: At 150% the multiplier is x2.5: a +12% Maximum Life jewel behaves like +30% Life, and every other qualifying jewel scales the same way. The bonus is additive increased Effect, not a flat absolute.
officialAnswer: A perfect 150% roll multiplies each Corrupted Magic Jewel's effect by 2.5.

problems.symptom: Character sheet did not change after equipping The Adorned

Confirm it is socketed in the passive tree inside the radius.
